children: Taiwan's export growth remained firm in August as the artificial-intelligence-driven boom settled into a steadier pace.
Shipments rose 41.0% in value from a year earlier, official data showed Wednesday, beating the 33.85% growth expected by economists polled by The Wall Street Journal.

Exports of electronic products rose 58% in August, while shipments of information and communications products expanded 42%. The U.S. remained Taiwan's largest export market, with shipments climbing 21%.

Taiwan's hardware makers, led by Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co., have become the backbone of the global build-out of AI infrastructure, boosting the island's exports of advanced technology. However, Taiwan's overall export growth has slowed in recent months from a peak of more than 60% earlier this year.

Economists have said the initial surge in demand for AI-related infrastructure is settling into a steadier cycle as tougher year-earlier comparisons emerge. Elevated global borrowing costs and uncertainty over tariff policies also pose risks to the sustainability of AI-related demand.
Investors will focus on interest-rate decisions from both the Federal Reserve and the Taiwanese central bank next week.

Wednesday's data also showed that imports rose 44.3% in August from a year earlier, accelerating from a 37.4% increase in July, as the Middle East conflict drove up energy prices. That took the trade surplus to US$22.30 billion.
